EE-001.note: The pinned census enumerates all 232 approved IDs with 32 adjustments, 16 drawings, 149 filters and 35 manipulations, 219 previewable and 13 immediate modes and 963 declared parameter controls; CensusCatalogTest verifies those totals and the uniqueness of every effect ID, parameter ID and parameter label. The native registry implements 172 of 232 registered: Adjustments 32/32, Drawings 16/16, Filters 91/149, Manipulations 33/35. The 60 approved IDs without a native implementation are 58 filters plus remove_background and scale. remove_background is not implemented because it awaits a product decision on an approved local model; the 58 filters and scale have no native implementation and no approved platform disposition. effect-catalog-selection.json still records status draft-selection-pending-product-owner-approval, so the explicit owner review of the ID set is not evidenced on this platform. Full catalog coverage and the owner-approved selection record remain Required.

EE-002.note: Effect IDs are registry keys and are independent of display name, localisation, icon and menu changes; EffectRegistry rejects an empty or duplicate ID and keeps a deterministic order. The browser supports category, search, recent and favorite discovery over the registered set without duplicating an ID, and the private effects store removes duplicate entries and drops unknown retired IDs instead of failing. The 60 approved census IDs without a native implementation cannot be discovered in the browser at all, so the browser does not yet cover the approved set. Complete browser coverage of all 232 IDs remains Required.

EE-004.note: A previewable effect runs through prepareEffectEdit on an OwnedWork worker with a cancellable non-authoritative preview. The document, pixels, annotations, history and dirty state are unchanged until Apply, and Apply commits exactly one history operation. Cancel and window close restore the exact prior document and leave Undo disabled. EffectsDialogTest proves the serialised document is equal to the pre-preview value while a preview is shown, that Cancel leaves the document equal to that pre-preview value, and that Apply produces one undo entry whose committed pixels equal the previewed pixels.

audit.coverage: Tested Linux candidate seam; native/physical/human qualification is not accepted by this classification.

EE-005.note: An immediate effect is applied through the same single guarded commit path and is reversible through one history entry; no effect performs an irreversible external action, so no confirmation gate is required. A failing effect reports the stable effect-failed code in the dialog status label and commits nothing. EffectsDialogTest verifies for a failing effect and for a cancelled apply that pixels, annotations, history, dirty state and the serialised document are exactly as they were before invocation.

audit.coverage: Tested Linux candidate seam; native/physical/human qualification is not accepted by this classification.

EE-006.note: prepareEffectEdit detects a size-changing result and prepares it through prepareCanvasEdit with CanvasAction::ResizeCanvas, so the centred canvas geometry, annotation protection and history rules of EDITOR-CANVAS-001 apply and the browser entry cannot bypass them. EffectsDialogTest compares the committed document with the geometry prepareCanvasEdit produces for the same operation and checks that the effect operation and its parameters and seed are recorded on it.

EE-008.note: Every registered effect exposes a seed derived from defaultEffectSeed(id). The browser shows the seed, offers a new seed and stores the accepted seed per effect in the private effects store, and the committed effect operation records the seed that produced the pixels. Procedural randomness uses a SplitMix64 generator seeded only from the effect context, never from time or a global generator. EffectFrameworkTest passes the seed through unchanged and proves that one seed repeats identical pixels while another seed does not, and EffectsDialogTest proves the persisted seed reloads and reproduces the previewed pixels. Identical decoded pixels on all supported platforms for the same seed, renderer version and colour profile are not proven on this platform. Audit 2026-11-03 (Aoife, at ef77af6): Procedural effects receive a persisted per-effect seed that is shown, can be renewed, is recorded on the committed operation and reproduces the preview; every registered effect is pixel-stable under a fixed seed. Cross-platform identity awaits the shared golden vectors. Remaining items above are qualification, not implementation status.

audit.coverage: Tested Linux candidate seam; native/physical/human qualification is not accepted by this classification.

EffectSupport defines straight-alpha centred Clamp convolution and premultiplied blur/unpremultiply behavior; DrawingEffectsTest::backgroundImageCoversTilesAndRejectsBadFiles proves tiled/covered/clipped image composition. Existing orientation is resolved during source preparation. EE-010.note: Preview and apply run on an OwnedWork worker that reports progress and honours cancellation; changed cancels the previous job and increments a revision so only the latest result is published, and the row driver in EffectSupport polls cancellation before every row. prepareEffectEdit rejects a source or result above the dimension, pixel-count or encoded-byte limits with effect-resource-limit, and a cancelled or abandoned preview never publishes a partial result. EffectFrameworkTest proves a cancelled run discards an otherwise successful image, and EffectsDialogTest proves Escape cancels the in-flight preview without committing and that only the newest preview is shown.

EE-011.note: Committing an effect goes through EditorSession::commitWithSelection, which truncates the history to the current position and so clears the redo branch; EffectsDialogTest commits a new effect after an Undo and observes redoCount 0. A preview never enters history, never dirties the document and never reorders the recent list: the document stays byte-equal while a preview is shown and the recent list is updated only on the successful commit path.

audit.coverage: Tested Linux candidate seam; native/physical/human qualification is not accepted by this classification.

EE-012.note: Recent and favourite entries are stable effect IDs. The private effects store removes duplicates, keeps a deterministic newest-first recent order capped at 20, drops unknown retired IDs instead of failing, and detects a concurrent change through its snapshot and reports effects-store-changed. The favourite control adds and removes an ID and the Recent and Favorites categories list only those IDs. The user-editable lists never change the effect catalog. Unknown retired IDs are discarded on load rather than retained.

audit.coverage: Tested Linux candidate seam; native/physical/human qualification is not accepted by this classification.

EE-014.note: The preview is rendered at full resolution by the same prepareEffectEdit path used by Apply; only the displayed pixmap is scaled down to the widget, so the preview pixels and the committed pixels are identical. EffectsDialogTest compares the previewed pixel with the committed pixel, and the status line states that the preview is not committed. No registered effect previews at reduced fidelity, so there is no bounded preview difference to disclose.

EE-015.note: An imported preset keeps unknown root, step and parameter JSON for round-trip and marks the step unsupported with a typed diagnostic; an invalid parameter value is kept verbatim and marked unsupported with effect-invalid-parameter. No reflection, script, network access or arbitrary constructor is involved: a preset is read as JSON and zip entries only. The archive reader refuses encrypted, multi-disk, overlapping, duplicate, malformed and over-limit archives with typed codes, and an imported path can only address an embedded asset.

EE-016.note: Effect execution is local. The registry, the census and the effect implementations read only the document, the local parameter values and local asset files, and nothing in the effect path opens a network connection. Preset assets are embedded in the document rather than fetched, and the committed document contains no host path.

EE-018.note: Every registered effect is a deterministic CPU and native Qt implementation, so the registered set declares no hardware codec, font or accelerator dependency. Where the environment does lack a capability, the effect reports a typed diagnostic instead of degrading silently: a text effect without a QGuiApplication for font resolution returns effect-unavailable, and an unreadable or oversized asset returns effect-invalid-input. Ubuntu/Qt 6.4.2 CI 40098357984 exposed use of QImage::flipped, introduced in Qt 6.9. Drawing reflections now call one EffectSupport helper selecting the minimum-supported API; asymmetric exact-pixel tests cover both axes and rotated reflections without altering any golden expectation. The corrective pushed revision must pass baseline CI before baseline compatibility is claimed. Audit 2026-11-03: No effect is silently omitted from the browser. Every census ID stays listed; each one without a native implementation (today only remove_background, which needs an approved local model) is a disabled entry carrying 'effect-unavailable: <reason>' in its text, tooltip and accessible text (EffectsDialogTest::unavailableCensusAndSearch asserts all 232 IDs are listed and each unavailable one is disabled with the typed diagnostic and reason), selecting one shows the same diagnostic in the status (unitsAndRuntimeUnavailable), and the dialog states the total up front with an accessible 'N effects unavailable on Linux' notice, a tooltip and an expandable list of every unavailable effect with its reason (EffectsDialogTest::unavailableEffectsAreSummarisedWithAnAccessibleExpandableList). Registered effects are deterministic CPU/native implementations with no hardware, codec, font or accelerator dependency; a missing font/native resource reports effect-unavailable. The earlier note that 60 census IDs were silently omitted was stale: the registered set now covers all but remove_background. The formal approved platform disposition for remove_background (model/device) remains a human decision recorded in audit.remaining_human_decision.
